messages:
perf-canary-bot: Canary summary posted for `runtime-1.19.0-canary.7` (scheduler_flag=on vs baseline)
• window: 2h
• scenario: mixed_workload_v2 (short chat + long-context summarization)
• p95 end-to-end latency: -17% (improved)
• p99 end-to-end latency: -6% (improved)
• throughput (tok/s): -3.4%
• GPU util: -2.1pp
• errors/timeouts: no change
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rt-mixed-workload-canary?var=build=runtime-1.19.0-canary.7

Aisha Bello: looking at the graphs now. p95 looks genuinely better (esp in the burst windows), but the tok/s dip is consistent across both regions.

Sean Gallagher: +1. question is whether the throughput dip is “real” (scheduler overhead / smaller batches) vs artifact (traffic mix / warmup). what’s our go/no-go criteria here?

Rafael Mendes: SRE view: p95 improvement is great, but if we take a sustained throughput hit we may just push queue depth higher in prod and lose the win. the queue depth panels show long-queue sitting higher than baseline.

Omar El-Sayed: I suspect batching is the culprit. with two queues, the short queue is getting serviced more frequently, which reduces batch sizes for decode. net result: better tail, slightly worse aggregate tok/s.

Peter Holtz: do we have the per-class batch size histograms from the new metrics? (short_batch_tokens / long_batch_tokens). if short batches are smaller and more frequent, that matches.

Aisha Bello: not seeing batch size hist yet in the canary dashboard (only queue depth + wait time + prefill/decode split). i can add a panel if the metric exists.

Sofia Ivanova: we don’t emit batch size directly right now. we do have `scheduler.dispatch.batch_tokens` in the sampled logs (PR 8502), and we can scrape a rough distribution from that.

Jonas Weber: for perf program purposes, i’m less worried about -3% tok/s if we can show it’s bounded and doesn’t worsen under higher load. but we need more data than 2h.

Sana Farid: +1. also want to see if the dip correlates with the long-prompt ratio. did the mix shift at all between A/B? if baseline got “luckier” on long prompts, we could be misreading.

Rina Kobayashi: canary job is doing A/B on the same incoming stream, but split is per-request routing so there is some variance. the trace replay benches had ~-1% tok/s, not -3.4%. i want to rerun with a longer window and pin the mix distribution.

Tomáš Novák: operationally: if we were to proceed, what’s the rollback trigger? i’d want an explicit “if tok/s down >X% AND queue depth trending up for Y mins” type rule.

Sean Gallagher: agree. propose:
- rollback if sustained tok/s regression >5% for 30 min OR long-queue depth grows monotonically for 20 min while p95 stops improving.
- also watch request timeouts (even if aggregate stable).

Aisha Bello: there’s also a mild increase in “time waiting in scheduler” for long class (median). not huge, but consistent.

Omar El-Sayed: that’s expected with fairness window. but should be bounded by max-wait guardrail. do we see `long_starvation_events` at all?

Aisha Bello: `scheduler.starvation_guardrail_triggered` is flat (0) in both. so not starving, just waiting a bit more.

Rafael Mendes: ok, but the long-queue depth is still higher. question: are we just deferring long prefills and keeping the system busy with short, which then reduces effective throughput? (context switching overhead)

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler overhead itself should be negligible (lock contention fix went in). more likely it’s the smaller effective batch sizes / less continuous batching on long prefills. we can try tuning the fairness window and weights.

Jonas Weber: before tuning, can we validate it’s not a measurement issue?
asks:
1) rerun canary window >= 8h to smooth traffic variance
2) run at two load levels (current + 20% synthetic) to see if regression grows
3) export a table: batch tokens distribution proxy from sampled logs

Sana Farid: and add p95 broken down by prefill vs decode. the “win” might be coming from prefill queueing reduction, but if decode suffers we need to know.

Omar El-Sayed: we have `prefill_ms` and `decode_ms` split in the runtime spans. i can extend the canary summary to include deltas for those.

Rina Kobayashi: i can set up a trace replay run tonight with the same build/flag and publish the comparison (baseline vs on) across: p50/p95/p99, tok/s, GPU util, and mix stats.

Tomáš Novák: if we don’t have enough confidence, we should keep the flag in canary only and not expand the slice yet.

Sean Gallagher: decision for now: no slice expansion today. request more data per above. once we have 8h canary + trace replay, we reconvene tomorrow.

Aisha Bello: i’ll add dashboard panels:
- prefill/decode p95 by class
- long-queue depth trend with an alert draft (non-paging)
will post links here.

Rafael Mendes: +1. also please annotate the graph with the build deploy time. i don’t see a clear marker.

Aisha Bello: will do.

Sofia Ivanova: i’ll pull a quick distribution from the sampled `scheduler.dispatch` logs and share percentiles for batch tokens (short/long) so we can confirm the batching hypothesis.

Sean Gallagher: thanks all. :thumbsup: ping here when the new canary window finishes + replay results are in.
